who: D. A. 'Don' Smith, historian of Britain, formerly Yale and subsequently Grinnell College, doctorate Yale.

evidence.says: Identifies D. A. 'Don' Smith as a British historian with a Yale doctorate who moved from an assistant professorship at Yale to Grinnell in 1970.
The candidate is Don G. Smith, author of Lon Chaney, Jr. (1995).
The candidate's expanded name is Daniel Elliott Huger Smith; the authority cites correspondence addressed to him in 1908 and the work Charles Fraser.
The candidate is Donald Kimball Smith, a medieval and Renaissance literature teacher at Iowa and later Kansas State, author of Nothing Disappears.
The candidate is Donnal Vore Smith, identified as holding a PhD on Chase and Civil War Politics (1931).
The candidate is Donald Eugene Smith, editor of Diary of Gaspar de Portola (1909) and coauthor of The United States of America, a History (1931).

notes: The Yale adviser is D. A. Smith. None of the five supplied authority identities matches his name and career.

who: Gregory Smith, historian of late antiquity at Central Michigan University since 2006, PhD history Harvard 2005.

evidence.says: Joined CMU in fall 2006; PhD history Harvard 2005; researches ancient ideas about the soul, air, breath and spirit.
The candidate is Gregory Overton Smith, editor of Perspectives on Public Space in Rome, from Antiquity to the Present Day (2013).
The volume's title page affiliates editor Gregory Smith with Cornell University's College of Architecture, Art and Planning, Rome Program.
The Rome scholar Gregory Smith trained in social anthropology at Oxford and studies Italian rural communities and peripheral urban environments.

notes: The candidate is the Rome social anthropologist, a different scholar from CMU's Harvard-trained historian of late antiquity.

who: Adam M. Sowards, environmental historian at the University of Idaho, PhD history Arizona State 2001.

evidence.says: August 2021 CV identifies Adam M. Sowards as an Idaho history professor, employed there since July 2003, with a history PhD from Arizona State in 2001.
The 2018 review credits Adam M Sowards, University of Idaho, and explicitly supplies ORCID 0000-0002-2376-3524.

notes: Exact doctorate and institution agree; the publisher directly connects the candidate ORCID to the Idaho historian.

who: Jake W. Spidle, historian of medicine and modern Europe at the University of New Mexico, PhD Stanford 1972.

evidence.says: UNM lists Jake Spidle as history faculty emeritus, with a Stanford PhD in modern European history in 1972 and Doctors of Medicine in New Mexico among his books.
LC identifies Jake W. Spidle, Jr. as the author of Doctors of Medicine in New Mexico (1986).
A 1987 institutional oral-history interview identifies interviewer Jake Spidle, PhD, Department of History, University of New Mexico.

notes: Exact doctorate matches, and the faculty page and LC authority identify the same book and author.

who: Steven M. Stowe, historian of the American South and medicine at Indiana University, PhD Stony Brook 1979.

evidence.says: IU's retirement tribute records Stowe's Stony Brook history PhD in 1979, his recruitment to Indiana in 1987, and his book Intimacy and Power in the Old South.
LC identifies Steven M. Stowe as author of Intimacy and Power in the Old South (1987), then affiliated with Penn State's Department of Humanities.
Indiana's 2014-2015 bulletin lists Steven Stowe, History, among professors emeriti.

notes: Exact PhD agrees; the institutional career and shared book connect the LC identity to the Indiana supervisor.

who: William H. TeBrake, medieval and environmental historian at the University of Maine, PhD Texas at Austin 1975.

evidence.says: The Maine graduate-program listing names William TeBrake, PhD Texas 1975, professor specializing in western European medieval history and environment.
The University of Maine history faculty directory identifies William H. TeBrake as professor emeritus.
LC expands William H. TeBrake to William Henry TeBrake and identifies him as author of Medieval Frontier.
William H. TeBrake describes his own research beginning in 1972, his Texas at Austin dissertation of 1975, and its development into Medieval Frontier: Culture and Ecology in Rijnland.

notes: The 2004 faculty listing matches the student's institution and year; doctorate and book identify the LC candidate.

who: Thomas N. Tentler, medieval and Reformation historian at the University of Michigan, PhD Harvard 1961.

evidence.says: Michigan's regents identify Thomas N. Tentler as history faculty from 1963 to 2000 and record his Harvard doctorate in 1961.
The department states that Mark Lotito, PhD 2011, was the last PhD student of Tom Tentler, its longtime Reformation historian.
LC identifies Thomas N. Tentler as author of Sin and Confession on the Eve of the Reformation (1977).

notes: Exact doctorate and direct departmental confirmation of Lotito's supervision establish the match; the candidate's LC name and field agree.

who: Brian Loring Villa, military historian at the University of Ottawa and author of Unauthorized Action: Mountbatten and the Dieppe Raid.

evidence.says: A May 2003 contribution identifies Brian Loring Villa as professor of history at the University of Ottawa.
The Oxford University Press book's author is Brian Loring Villa; its author description identifies Brian Villa as associate professor of history at the University of Ottawa.
LC identifies Brian Loring Villa from the title page of Unauthorized Action (1989).

notes: Full name, Ottawa history affiliation close to the student's period, and the same book connect the candidate to the supervisor. The doctorate year was not independently verified.
